headline: Showers end Saturday evening, then clear, cold nights bring the season's first frost; light rain returns Tuesday into Wednesday.
summary: A weak low pressure system keeps scattered showers going through Saturday afternoon, with highs in the mid to upper 50s. Tonight, winds that gusted 20 to 35 mph are at their peak and should slowly ease. Lingering evening rain is mostly in a convergence zone (a narrow band where air flows together and produces rain) stretching from the Seattle area east into the Cascades, and it should weaken and drift south and east. Skies should clear Saturday evening. With clear skies and light winds, the ground will cool quickly, and Saturday night lows range from the mid 40s in the Seattle metro area to the mid 30s in sheltered valleys. The first Frost Advisory of the season runs from midnight Saturday night to 8 AM Sunday for the foothills and valleys of Pierce, southern King, Thurston and Lewis counties and the middle Chehalis River Valley. It could be expanded, though wind may keep frost from forming farther north in King and Snohomish counties, and fog near Olympia and Chehalis could complicate frost there. Breezy northeast winds, with gusts around 25 mph, are expected in western Whatcom County and the San Juans. Sunday looks drier and sunnier, with highs in the upper 50s to low 60s and more frost possible Sunday night. Monday should be mostly dry with highs in the low 60s and morning lows in the mid to upper 30s for most areas. A weak system should bring light rain Tuesday into Wednesday, with timing now later than earlier forecasts. After midweek the pattern is uncertain, but a return to high pressure and mild weather is considered most likely. Seas stay above 10 feet on the coast through midday Saturday, and a Gale Warning for the central and eastern Strait of Juan de Fuca runs until 11 PM tonight.
changes: Early on, forecasters focused on morning rain, wind and a cool weekend with possible frost. By midday they had issued the season's first Frost Advisory for Saturday night and noted rain mostly ended apart from a Seattle-to-Cascades shower band. By evening the midweek system looked later and weaker (light rain Tuesday into Wednesday), and the Frost Advisory was described as covering mainly the southwest Washington foothills and the middle Chehalis Valley, with possible expansion.
